title: The House Beside the Synagogue to the Hill That Took His Name
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Pest, birth on Dohany utca
stops.date_confidence: attested; day and place standard across reference works. Coordinate corrected in verification to the Dohany Street Synagogue's own pin, 47.49583 N 19.06083 E, and the district corrected from Belvaros to Erzsebetvaros, the VIIth.
stops.campa: In a two-storey Classicist house on Dohany utca, wall to wall with the great synagogue whose domes stand over the Jewish quarter of Pest, Jakob and Jeanette Herzl have a son and name him Theodor. The household is Neolog: modernizing, German-speaking in a Hungarian city, keeping selected rites and no Orthodoxy. The plot where the house stood will be built over in 1930 by the Hungarian Jewish Museum, and the museum joined to the synagogue the year after. By then the house itself is gone.
sources: en.wikipedia.org, 'Dohany Street Synagogue' (coordinates and the Jewish Museum built on the Herzl house plot)
suggested_refs: The Hungarian Jewish Museum, Dohany Street, standing on the site of the Herzl birth house

stops.name: Pest, the death of his sister Pauline
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia, 'Theodor Herzl'); the family's departure for Vienna is attested to the year 1878 only.
stops.campa: Pauline Herzl, his only sibling, dies of typhus on the seventh of February. The family does not stay. Within months the house beside the synagogue is given up and the Herzls leave Hungary for Vienna, carrying the grave with them as the reason. Her name will be given to his own first child twelve years later, and, seventy-one years after that, to a coffin flown out of Vienna beside his. Theodor is seventeen when they go. Nothing in the record says he objected and nothing says he wanted to go.
suggested_refs: The Jewish cemetery of Pest, first burial place of Pauline Herzl

stops.name: Vienna, the family resettles in the Alsergrund
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Wikipedia, 'Theodor Herzl', confirming the 1878 move to the 9th district); month and day defaulted, no source gives them.
stops.campa: The family settles in the ninth district, among the doctors' apartments and hospital streets north of where the old walls stood. He will see Budapest again; he will not live in Hungary again. Vienna in 1878 is the capital of a liberal empire in which Jewish families like this one have been legally emancipated for eleven years and are moving into law, medicine and the press as fast as the professions will take them. Herzl enrolls at the university to read law.
suggested_refs: The Alsergrund, Vienna's ninth district, the Herzl family's quarter after 1878

stops.name: Vienna, the fraternity Albia and the Wagner memorial
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the dossier as standard biographical scholarship (Kornberg, Pawel); the verification pass could not re-fetch a primary academic page for the Albia episode and flagged it as needing a direct source check. Month and day are inferred from Wagner's death in February 1883 and are not attested.
stops.campa: He joins Albia, a German-nationalist student fraternity under the motto Honor, Freedom, Fatherland, and fences and drinks with it as a Viennese law student does. He is twenty-two and has believed himself an ordinary member of it. In March the fraternity holds a memorial for Richard Wagner, dead a month, and the speeches turn openly antisemitic. Herzl resigns his membership. It is the first political act recorded of him, and the record does not say what he said on the way out.
stops.quote: Modern Anti-Semitism is not to be confounded with the religious persecution of the Jews of former times.
stops.quote_source: Der Judenstaat / The Jewish State (1896), section 'Causes of Anti-Semitism', written thirteen years later
sources: Dossier note attributed to standard biographical scholarship (Kornberg, Pawel), consistent with Wikipedia's education summary
Jewish Virtual Library, excerpts from Der Judenstaat
suggested_refs: The records of the Burschenschaft Albia, Vienna, 1881-1883

stops.name: Vienna, Doctor of Law
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; Wikipedia's education section, consistent across standard biographies.
stops.campa: On the sixteenth of May he takes his Doctor of Law from the University of Vienna. The degree is the correct end of a correct education, a professional credential for a merchant family's son and a passport into the courts of the empire. He will keep the title for life and sign with it, Dr. Herzl, on letters to sultans, grand dukes and popes, who will read it as the mark of a serious man rather than of a journalist. He practices law for one more year.
suggested_refs: The University of Vienna law faculty rolls, doctorate conferred 16 May 1884

stops.name: Salzburg, the last year in the law
stops.date_confidence: the practice ran August 1884 to June 1885 in Vienna and Salzburg per de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodor_Herzl; dating to 1885 alone marks only the end. The Salzburg posting and the specific courthouse could not be independently confirmed and the geography lens carries this as reconstruction.
stops.campa: Judicial practice runs from August of one year to June of the next, in Vienna and then here, under the Alps and the archbishops' palaces. He is twenty-five when it ends and he does not stay in the law. The reason he gives afterwards has never needed elaboration: as a Jew he could not have risen to a judgeship in the Austrian courts. He goes to the feuilleton instead, the short signed essay at the foot of the newspaper page, and makes his name in it.
sources: de.wikipedia.org, 'Theodor Herzl' (judicial practice August 1884 to June 1885, Vienna and Salzburg)
suggested_refs: The provincial court of Salzburg, place of his judicial year

stops.name: Vienna, the books of feuilletons
stops.date_confidence: years attested from the standard Herzl bibliography (Hagenau 1881, Neues von der Venus 1887, Das Buch der Narrheit 1888); month and day defaulted. The verification pass carries the early literary work as reconstruction, not as a claim checked against a fetched primary edition.
stops.campa: Hagenau came out in 1881, while he was still a student. Now the volumes accumulate: Neues von der Venus in 1887, Das Buch der Narrheit the following year. The pieces are light and exact and unmistakably his own, the work of a man who has found his form early, is admired for it, and is not important. Eight years separate this desk from the desk at which he writes Der Judenstaat, and the prose style he has by 1888 is the one he will use there. He is twenty-eight.
sources: Standard Herzl bibliography, consistent with the works list in Wikipedia, 'Theodor Herzl'
suggested_refs: Neues von der Venus (1887) and Das Buch der Narrheit (1888), the feuilleton collections

stops.name: Reichenau an der Rax, the marriage to Julie Naschauer
stops.date_confidence: date and town attested by de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodor_Herzl, '25. Juni 1889 in Reichenau an der Rax'; note that English Wikipedia wrongly gives Vienna. The venue, the Rudolfsvilla, is demoted to reconstruction: the Reichenau article describes that villa as the former imperial summer house and makes no connection to Herzl's wedding. Coordinate corrected to 47.69944 N 15.84484 E.
stops.campa: He marries Julie Naschauer, daughter of a wealthy Jewish business family, on the twenty-fifth of June in the Alpine resort town where Vienna's money summers. The marriage is unhappy early and stays unhappy for fifteen years. Which house they married in is not settled: the tradition names the Rudolfsvilla, and the Rudolfsvilla's own record knows nothing of them. Reichenau will hold both ends of his adult life. He is married here at twenty-nine and dies in this valley at forty-four.
sources: de.wikipedia.org, 'Reichenau an der Rax' (which confirms the 1889 marriage in the town but not the Rudolfsvilla)
suggested_refs: The Rudolfsvilla at Reichenau an der Rax, the traditional but uncorroborated wedding venue

stops.name: Paris, correspondent of the Neue Freie Presse
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested (Wikipedia, 'Theodor Herzl'); day defaulted. The bureau's exact address could not be located and the coordinate is an approximate right-bank pin.
stops.campa: The Neue Freie Presse, the most powerful liberal daily in the empire, sends him to Paris as its correspondent in October. He covers the Chamber of Deputies, the Panama scandals, anarchist bombings and the antisemitism running loudly through French public life, and he writes all of it in the feuilleton manner. The paper is read from Vienna to Trieste, and his signature at the foot of the column is known in both cities. Three children arrive in four years: Pauline in 1890, Hans in 1891, Trude in 1893.
suggested_refs: The Paris dispatches of the Neue Freie Presse, 1891-1895

stops.name: Vienna, a plan for a mass baptism
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The dossier characterizes this from Herzl's private papers; this session could not confirm the primary document beyond that characterization. Year as given by the dossier, month and day defaulted, and the whole item is carried as tradition rather than as document.
stops.campa: Before the Zionist years there is a stranger proposal, worked out in private and then abandoned: a spectacular collective conversion of the Jews to Christianity, carried out in the open and in a single generation, the fathers left where they are and the children taken over. He never attempts it. He never publishes it. It survives among his own papers as the furthest point to which the assimilationist answer could be pushed before it broke in his hands.
stops.quote: We have honestly endeavored everywhere to merge ourselves in the social life of surrounding communities
stops.quote_source: Der Judenstaat / The Jewish State (1896), 'Introduction', 1896 English translation attributed to Sylvie D'Avigdor
sources: Reconstruction from Herzl's private papers as characterized in the reviewed dossier, not independently verified against a primary document
Jewish Virtual Library, excerpts from Der Judenstaat
suggested_refs: The Herzl diaries and private papers, Central Zionist Archives, Jerusalem

stops.name: Vienna, Das neue Ghetto
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the standard Herzl bibliography and consistent with Wikipedia's account of his pre-Zionist writing; month and day defaulted, and no source fetched here fixes the weeks of composition.
stops.campa: He writes a play about an assimilated Jewish lawyer who does everything correctly, marries well, takes the right briefs, and discovers that the walls of the ghetto have not come down but have turned invisible and social. It ends in a duel. The argument of Der Judenstaat is already entirely present here, in stage dialogue, before he has any notion of a congress or a charter and before he has met anyone who agrees with him. No Vienna theatre will touch the play; it is first performed in 1898, four years after he writes it.
sources: Standard Herzl bibliography, consistent with Wikipedia, 'Theodor Herzl'
suggested_refs: Das neue Ghetto (1894), first performed in Vienna in 1898

stops.name: Paris, the arrest of Captain Dreyfus
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested (Wikipedia, 'Theodor Herzl'); day defaulted. The coordinate is inherited byte-identical from captain_alfred_dreyfus.journey.json, which pins this scene at 48.8566, 2.3522; note that this is a central-Paris pin, roughly two kilometres from the Ecole Militaire.
stops.campa: In October a captain of the French general staff, Alfred Dreyfus, the only Jew on it, is arrested for treason. Herzl the correspondent files on the case as it moves. He is thirty-four, with three small children and a play no theatre will stage. It is not yet the Affair. It is a spy story, and the Paris press treats the man's Jewishness as the natural explanation of the crime, in the capital of the first country in Europe to have emancipated its Jews.
suggested_refs: The Neue Freie Presse dispatches on the Dreyfus arrest, October 1894

stops.name: Paris, the courtyard and the broken sword
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. German Wikipedia confirms Herzl was personally present at the 5 January 1895 ceremony; the Ecole Militaire article does not itself mention the degradation, so the building attribution rests on general history. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from captain_alfred_dreyfus.journey.json rather than the corrected Ecole Militaire pin of 48.85250, 2.30361.
stops.campa: On a January morning, before assembled troops, Dreyfus is stripped of his rank, his braid torn from the sleeve, his sword broken, and marched down the ranks while a crowd shouts beyond the railings. Herzl is present and reports it. Four years later he writes that the case carried a wish to condemn all Jews in one Jew. Whether he stood at the railings himself his own papers do not settle, and whether the crowd was shouting Death to the traitor or Death to the Jews they do not settle either.
stops.quote: Are we to 'get out' now and where to?
stops.quote_source: Der Judenstaat / The Jewish State (1896), section 'The Jewish Question'
sources: Jewish Virtual Library, excerpts from Der Judenstaat
suggested_refs: The degradation ceremony in the courtyard of the Ecole Militaire, 5 January 1895

stops.name: Paris, the refusal of Baron Hirsch
stops.date_confidence: contested and not resolved here. The dossier gives 3 June 1895; de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodor_Herzl places the meeting in May 1895; standard Herzl scholarship dates it 2 June 1895. The date shown is the scholarly one, chosen only to order the segment. The Paris location is an inference, not confirmed by any fetched source.
stops.campa: He asks for and gets an audience with Baron Maurice de Hirsch, the richest Jewish philanthropist in Europe. Herzl brings a long memorandum and a manner better suited to a stage. Hirsch listens, objects, and refuses him. Herzl walks out and starts writing at speed, no longer addressing a financier but everybody, in the room, in the street, on trains. He begins the diary in the same weeks and keeps it until three weeks before he dies. De.wikipedia dates the finished manuscript to the seventeenth of June.
stops.quote: The Jewish question still exists. It would be foolish to deny it.
sources: de.wikipedia.org, 'Theodor Herzl' (Hirsch meeting May 1895; manuscript completed 17 June 1895)
Jewish Virtual Library, excerpts from Der Judenstaat
suggested_refs: The memorandum for Baron Maurice de Hirsch, June 1895
Herzl-Online (herzlonline.org), facsimiles of the eighteen diaries, June 1895 to May 1904

stops.name: Vienna and Leipzig, Der Judenstaat
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the Project Gutenberg edition of The Jewish State confirms 14 February 1896, published by M. Breitenstein simultaneously in Vienna and Leipzig. The weighing of Argentina against Palestine inside the text is carried as reconstruction: this session confirmed it only from the dossier, not from a fetched page of the pamphlet itself.
stops.campa: Der Judenstaat: Versuch einer modernen Loesung der Judenfrage appears on the fourteenth of February, in Vienna and Leipzig at once. The argument is cold and administrative. Antisemitism is not a medieval residue that education dissolves but a standing condition of Jewish life among nations, and the answer is sovereignty: a chartered territory, a company, an exodus organized like a railway timetable. Two countries are weighed in the text, Argentina and Palestine, and the pamphlet does not settle between them.
stops.quote_source: The Jewish State (Der Judenstaat), 'Introduction', 1896 English translation attributed to Sylvie D'Avigdor
sources: Project Gutenberg edition of The Jewish State
suggested_refs: M. Breitenstein's Verlags-Buchhandlung first edition, Vienna and Leipzig, 14 February 1896

stops.name: Vienna, the chaplain at the British Embassy
stops.date_confidence: the meeting date is carried from the dossier and attested in Wikipedia's Herzl chronology; the embassy's exact 1896 address and its identity as the meeting site are not confirmed by any source fetched here, so the coordinate is approximate.
stops.campa: William Henry Hechler, Anglican chaplain to the British embassy, millenarian, calculator of prophetic dates, has read the pamphlet and comes looking for its author. He holds that the return of the Jews to Palestine is scheduled in scripture for this generation and that he has found the man appointed to it. He had been tutor to the house of Baden, which means he can reach a grand duke, and through a grand duke a Kaiser. Herzl needs doors, and this is the man who has them. He accepts him and keeps him for the rest of his life.
suggested_refs: Hechler's correspondence with the court of Baden on Herzl's behalf, 1896

stops.name: Karlsruhe, the Grand Duke of Baden
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The audience is carried from the dossier; the exact palace and the date were not independently verified this session. Month and day are chosen only to order the segment between the Hechler meeting in March and the Constantinople journey in June.
stops.campa: Hechler's introduction puts him in front of Frederick I, Grand Duke of Baden, uncle of the German Emperor. The Grand Duke is courteous and curious, and he is the first reigning sovereign in Europe to receive the Vienna journalist as the representative of anything at all. Nothing is promised. But the line now runs chaplain to grand duke to Berlin, and Herzl has learned the working principle of the next eight years: the courts of Europe will open to a man who behaves as though he already governs a people.
sources: Dossier, carried as reconstruction; not independently re-verified this session
suggested_refs: The court of Frederick I of Baden, Karlsruhe, first princely audience of the Zionist campaign

stops.name: Constantinople, the Porte and the intermediary
stops.date_confidence: the visit ran 15 to 29 June 1896 (Wikipedia); the date shown is the arrival, not a meeting date. Coordinate corrected to the Sublime Porte at approximately 41.0119 N 28.9790 E, replacing a pin that fell near the Grand Bazaar. Verification found no support for the claim that Herzl himself met Grand Vizier Halil Rifat Pasha.
stops.campa: He travels to the Ottoman capital with Philipp Michael von Newlinski, a Polish nobleman with access to the palace, carrying a single offer: Jewish finance to consolidate the Ottoman public debt, in exchange for a charter of settlement in Palestine. The Sultan does not receive him. Newlinski carries the proposal in and brings the answer back out. As long as I am alive, Abdulhamid says, I will not have our body divided; only our corpse can they divide.
sources: en.wikipedia.org, 'Abdul Hamid II' (Newlinski's audience and the Sultan's refusal)
suggested_refs: The Bab-i Ali, the Sublime Porte, seat of the Ottoman government in 1896

stops.name: Whitechapel, the meeting in the East End
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia, 'Theodor Herzl'); the specific club or hall and its address come from the dossier and were not independently pinpointed. The English translation of the pamphlet, published in London that May, is attested to the month only.
stops.campa: London's Jewish grandees have received him coolly, and the men who could fund him are among them. The English translation has been on sale in the city for two months. Then in the East End, in a hall packed with immigrant tailors and cabinetmakers out of Russia and Poland, the constituency his pamphlet reasoned its way to is standing in front of him, in a room, on its feet, and it has no money to give him. He speaks, and the ovation that answers him does not stop.
stops.quote: It is precisely the poorest whom we need at first. Only the desperate make good conquerors.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Theodor Herzl' (12 July 1896 East End rally; English translation, London, May 1896)
suggested_refs: The Jewish Working Men's Club, Whitechapel, traditional site of the 12 July 1896 meeting

stops.name: Munich, the congress that cannot meet there
stops.date_confidence: year attested; Wikipedia's 'First Zionist Congress' confirms Munich as the original planned site before relocation. Month and day are defaulted, no source fetched here dates the rabbis' protest exactly.
stops.campa: The first congress is to meet in Munich. The German rabbinate publishes a protest against the whole undertaking: the effort to found a Jewish national state contradicts the messianic promise, and Judaism obliges its adherents to the fatherland they belong to. Herzl answers with a coinage, Protestrabbiner, protest rabbis, and moves the congress across the border to Switzerland. The first organized opposition to the undertaking is Jewish, and it is in print before a single delegate has arrived anywhere.
suggested_refs: The 1897 declaration of the Executive Committee of the German Rabbis against the Zionist congress

stops.name: Vienna, Die Welt is founded
stops.date_confidence: founding date attested (Wikipedia, 'Theodor Herzl'); the paper's exact Vienna office address could not be located, so the coordinate is a city-centre pin.
stops.campa: The established Jewish press in Vienna will not carry the movement, so on the fourth of June he founds a weekly of his own. Die Welt is propaganda organ, news service and correspondence bureau at once, and two months later it is the paper of record for the congress at Basel. It is also a permanent hole in his household accounts. He covers the deficits himself, out of a journalist's salary, year after year, while the Neue Freie Presse that pays that salary will not print a line about Zionism.
sources: Dossier, for the personal financing of the paper (carried as reconstruction)
suggested_refs: Die Welt, Vienna, 1897-1914, the Zionist Organization's weekly

stops.name: Basel, the Stadtcasino and the First Congress
stops.date_confidence: attested; the congress ran 29 to 31 August 1897 in the Musiksaal of the Stadtcasino on the Steinenberg. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from martin_buber.journey.json and samuel_preiswerk.journey.json; de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadtcasino_Basel gives 47.554444, 7.589444, about 300 m away, and that discrepancy is left standing rather than silently corrected.
stops.campa: Around two hundred delegates, in formal evening dress on his insistence, in the Musiksaal on the Steinenberg. He has staged all of it, the dress, the photographers, the order of business, as an act of state performed by a state that does not exist, and the delegates comply. They adopt the Basel Program: Zionism seeks to establish a home for the Jewish people in Palestine secured under public law. They constitute the Zionist Organization and elect Herzl president of it.
stops.quote: Let the sovereignty be granted us over a portion of the globe large enough to satisfy the rightful requirements of a nation
stops.quote_source: The Jewish State (1896 translation), section 'The Plan'
sources: Jewish Virtual Library, excerpts from Der Judenstaat
samuel_preiswerk.journey.json, for the Basel restorationist precedent Herzl invoked
suggested_refs: The Basel Program, adopted 29-31 August 1897

Samuel Preiswerk of Basel, who argued for Jewish settlement in Palestine twenty-six years before the congress met in his city and died when Herzl was eleven; no meeting is possible and none is claimed

stops.name: Vienna, the diary entry of the third of September
stops.date_confidence: attested and now traced to the primary text. The Complete Diaries of Theodor Herzl, ed. Raphael Patai, tr. Harry Zohn (Herzl Press, 1960), vol. II p. 581, under the heading 'September 3. Vienna'. The entry is written in Vienna three days after the congress closed, not in Basel; Zohn spells the city Basel, not the older British Basle.
stops.campa: Three days after the congress closes, at his own desk in Vienna, he writes the sentence down and in the same breath forbids himself to say it aloud. He gives it five years, or fifty. The diary is where the enterprise is kept honest; the public man never speaks like this. Then he adds a second line that is almost never quoted with the first: that what he made at Basel is an abstraction, and that an abstraction is invisible to most people. The entry is headed September 3, Vienna.
stops.quote: Were I to sum up the Basel Congress in a word -- which I shall guard against pronouncing publicly -- it would be this: At Basel I founded the Jewish State. If I said this out loud today, I would be answered by universal laughter. Perhaps in five years, and certainly in fifty, everyone will know it.
stops.quote_source: The Complete Diaries of Theodor Herzl, ed. Raphael Patai, tr. Harry Zohn (Herzl Press, 1960), vol. II, p. 581, entry headed 'September 3. Vienna'
sources: The Complete Diaries of Theodor Herzl, vol. II p. 581, read from the scanned text at archive.org/details/TheCompleteDiariesOfTheodorHerzl_201606
suggested_refs: The diary manuscript for 3 September 1897, Central Zionist Archives, published in facsimile by Herzl-Online

stops.name: Basel, the Second Congress
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested (standard Zionist Congress records; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Zionist_Congress confirms Basel, August 1898). The day is defaulted to open the session and is not attested here. Coordinate inherited as at the First Congress.
stops.campa: The movement meets again on the Steinenberg, larger, with delegates now grouped by country and a program of finance and colonization to fight over. The questions that will eventually split it are already on the floor: whether to buy land quietly or wait for a charter, whether culture or diplomacy comes first, whether this is a parliament or an instrument in one man's hands. Herzl chairs from the front. The bank he needs is voted through and incorporated the following year in London.
stops.quote: My proposal could only be carried out with the free consent of a majority of Jews.
sources: Wikipedia, 'First Zionist Congress' (Stadtcasino as recurring venue)
suggested_refs: Proceedings of the Second Zionist Congress, Basel, August 1898

stops.name: Jaffa, the landing
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Jaffa is widely attested as the arrival point of the 1898 trip, but the dedicated Wikipedia page on the journey returned a 404 this session and the port landing could not be independently confirmed beyond the dossier. Month attested from the Mikveh Israel meeting of 29 October; the day shown is chosen only to precede it.
stops.campa: He lands at Jaffa in October, the only time in his life he sets foot in the country he has been writing about for three years. The crossing has been brutal: heat, seasickness, a heart already failing him at thirty-eight. What he sets down is admiring and repelled at once, the landscape overwhelming him, the towns filthy in his account, a European's notebook on an Ottoman province he means to reorganize. He is in Palestine for less than two weeks and never comes back.
sources: Dossier, carried as reconstruction; the dedicated Wikipedia page on Herzl's 1898 journey returned 404 this session
suggested_refs: The port of Jaffa, landing point of the October 1898 journey

stops.name: Mikveh Israel, the Kaiser at the school gate
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day and to the exact spot; Wikipedia's 'Mikveh Israel' confirms the meeting took place at the main entrance of the school.
stops.campa: At the main entrance of the agricultural school founded in 1870, in the dust of the road, Herzl waits with a small delegation for the imperial party to come up. Wilhelm II reins in his horse and speaks with him for a few minutes about water and settlement, and rides on. The encounter is engineered as a press event and works as one: the wire services carry it across Europe as German interest in a Jewish Palestine. The exchange itself took a few minutes at a gate, in the dust, and settled nothing.
stops.quote: Labor without enterprise is the stationary labor of ancient days.
sources: arthur_balfour.journey.json, which records the same school shown to Balfour on his 1925 Palestine tour
suggested_refs: The main entrance of the Mikveh Israel agricultural school, founded 1870

stops.name: Jerusalem, through the Jaffa Gate
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The association of the 1898 imperial visit with the Jaffa Gate is general history and was not confirmed by any source fetched this session; the day shown is chosen only to place him in the city before the audience of 2 November.
stops.campa: He goes into the Old City through the Jaffa Gate in the days when the Kaiser's ceremonial entry is being staged through the same walls. He has a fever. He finds the city encrusted, airless, ruined by centuries of superstition and filth, and he writes down a plan to build a new Jerusalem outside the walls and leave the old one to the priests. He is walking through the capital of the thing he is arguing for. The argument is a document; the city is not.
sources: General historical association of the 1898 imperial visit with the Jaffa Gate; not independently confirmed by a fetched source
suggested_refs: The Jaffa Gate and the Old City walls, opened for the imperial visit of 1898

stops.name: Jerusalem, the tent camp on the Street of the Prophets
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia, 'Theodor Herzl', 'Street of the Prophets tent camp, 2 November 1898'). The claim that the famous photograph of the two men is a later composite is carried from the dossier and was not independently re-verified.
stops.campa: The formal audience is granted on the second of November, in a tent encampment pitched for the imperial tour on the Street of the Prophets outside the walls. Herzl reads an address. The Kaiser answers in general terms about a land that needs water and shade, and commits to nothing whatsoever. It is the highest point Herzl's diplomacy ever reaches and it produces no document. The photograph of the two men together is said to have been assembled afterwards from separate frames.
sources: Dossier, for the composite-photograph claim, flagged as unverified
suggested_refs: The imperial tent camp on the Street of the Prophets, Jerusalem, November 1898

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Western Wall
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and weakly held. This session could not confirm the visit or locate the diary passage in the portions of the Complete Diaries text it could read. The date is chosen only to close the Jerusalem days; the dossier gives the visit no date at all.
stops.campa: Tradition puts him at the Wall in these days, and reports that what he set down afterwards was distaste: for the beggars, the noise, the ecstasy of strangers at a ruin. The passage is quoted by his admirers as the honesty of a modernizer and by his opponents as contempt for the people already living the religion he proposed to give a country. Which of the two readings the page supports is a question the page would settle, if the page could be laid on a table.
sources: Widely repeated in the Herzl literature; unverified in this session against the Complete Diaries text available
suggested_refs: The Complete Diaries, October-November 1898, for the disputed Western Wall passage

stops.name: London, the Jewish Colonial Trust
stops.date_confidence: year attested from the reviewed dossier and consistent with general Zionist institutional history; month and day are defaulted and no source fetched here gives the incorporation date. The City address could not be located and the coordinate is approximate.
stops.campa: The Jewish Colonial Trust is incorporated in London, the movement's bank and the instrument through which any future charter would be paid for. The great Jewish financiers do not subscribe. The capital comes in slowly, in single-pound shares, from small subscribers who can barely spare the pound. The bank works exactly as designed, and it never reaches the sum Herzl would need to lay in front of a sultan. No charter is ever put in front of it to pay for.
stops.quote: All our material welfare has been brought about by men of enterprise.
sources: Reviewed dossier, consistent with general Zionist-institutional history
suggested_refs: The Jewish Colonial Trust (Juedische Colonialbank), incorporated in London, 1899

stops.name: Vienna, the answer to Yusuf Diya al-Khalidi
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. Two dates must not be collapsed: al-Khalidi's letter to Chief Rabbi Zadoc Kahn is dated 1 March 1899, and Herzl's reply to al-Khalidi is 19 March 1899. Only the reply belongs at this pin and this date.
stops.campa: Yusuf Diya al-Khalidi, former mayor of Jerusalem, has written to the Chief Rabbi of France on the first of March. The idea is natural and just in the abstract, he writes, but Palestine is inhabited, and the country would have to be taken by force from people already living in it. On the nineteenth Herzl replies to him directly from Vienna. He denies that Jewish immigration could dispossess anyone, argues that the newcomers will enrich the population already there, and leaves the objection where it stands.
suggested_refs: Yusuf Diya al-Khalidi to Zadoc Kahn, 1 March 1899, and Herzl's reply of 19 March 1899

stops.name: London, the Fourth Congress
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The month and year are carried from the dossier's chronology; the exact London venue could not be located this session and the day is defaulted to open the session. The coordinate is a central-London pin, not a hall.
stops.campa: The Fourth Congress meets in London, the only one of the first six held outside Basel, chosen because Britain is where the Jewish refugee question is being argued in public and where a government might actually be listening. Herzl is a public figure in England now, and from here, not from Constantinople, the last four years of his diplomacy will run. On the floor the debates are on Romania, on the Russian emigration, and on where the money is going.
sources: Dossier chronology, carried as reconstruction; exact venue not located this session
suggested_refs: Proceedings of the Fourth Zionist Congress, London, August 1900

stops.name: Constantinople, Yildiz Palace and the audience
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdul_Hamid_II confirms the date, Vambery's mediating role and the debt-administration dispute. The palace is not named in that source; the coordinate has been corrected to Yildiz Palace, Abdul Hamid's residence, 41.04944 N 29.01111 E, replacing a pin some 5.5 km away.
stops.campa: Five years after the first attempt, through the mediation of Armin Vambery, the Hungarian orientalist who has the Sultan's ear, Abdulhamid II receives him on the seventeenth of May. Herzl offers a syndicate that would lift the Ottoman public debt out of European hands and return its administration to the Sultan. Abdulhamid wants the money question kept separate from any question of colonization, and gets his way. There is no charter. There will not be one.
suggested_refs: Yildiz Palace, Abdul Hamid II's residence and seat of audiences after 1877

stops.name: Vienna, Die Welt handed to Martin Buber
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested in martin_buber.journey.json; day defaulted. The February 1900 first meeting between the two men is likewise attested in Buber's file, which does not pin its location more precisely than Vienna. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from martin_buber.journey.json.
stops.campa: He hands the editorship of Die Welt to Martin Buber, twenty-three, whom he had not met face to face until February of the year before and who came into the movement through Nathan Birnbaum's cultural wing rather than his own diplomatic one. Herzl wants a political weekly. Buber fills the paper with art, Hebrew renaissance, the Jewish spirit rather than the Jewish state. Within months the two of them are in open disagreement, and the disagreement is not personal but structural. Buber gives up the editorship the following year.
suggested_refs: Die Welt under Buber's editorship, September 1901 to 1902

stops.name: Basel, the Fifth Congress and the Democratic Faction
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the reviewed dossier and standard institutional history place the Jewish National Fund authorization at the Fifth Congress in Basel, dated by the geography lens to December 1901. The day is defaulted to open the session. Coordinate inherited as at the First Congress.
stops.campa: The Fifth Congress votes the Jewish National Fund into existence: a land-purchase instrument funded by small collections, holding whatever it buys inalienably in the name of the people. In the same hall the Democratic Faction organizes against Herzl, Buber among them, demanding cultural work, democratic control, and an end to a movement run out of one man's private correspondence. Herzl carries the vote on the fund. He does not answer the charge.
sources: Reviewed dossier, consistent with standard Zionist Organization institutional history
suggested_refs: The founding resolution of the Jewish National Fund, Fifth Zionist Congress, Basel, 1901

stops.name: Leipzig, Altneuland
stops.date_confidence: year attested; Wikipedia's 'Altneuland' confirms publication in 1902 by Hermann Seemann Nachfolger in Leipzig and Nahum Sokolow's Hebrew translation the same year in Warsaw under the title Tel Aviv. Month and day are defaulted, no fetched source gives them.
stops.campa: Six years after the pamphlet, the novel: a Jewish Palestine of 1923, cooperative, multilingual, electrified, its Arab citizens enfranchised and content, its opera houses full every night. It is a program dressed as fiction and a reply to everyone who called Der Judenstaat impossible. Nahum Sokolow's Hebrew translation appears the same year in Warsaw under the title Tel Aviv, mound of spring. Eight years later, settlers north of Jaffa take that name for their new town.
stops.quote: If you will it, It is no fable.
stops.quote_source: Old-New Land (Altneuland), title-page motto, tr. Lotta Levensohn, New York: Bloch Publishing Co., 1941, the first full English translation
suggested_refs: Altneuland (Leipzig, 1902) and Sokolow's Hebrew Tel Aviv (Warsaw, 1902)

stops.name: El-Arish, the water that is not there
stops.date_confidence: the El-Arish negotiation ran 1902-1903 (Wikipedia, 'Theodor Herzl'); month and day are chosen only to order the segment. The Royal Commission testimony and the meetings with Chamberlain, Lansdowne and Cromer are carried from the dossier and were not independently confirmed this session.
stops.campa: The British open a door: not Palestine, which is Ottoman, but the Sinai, on the Egyptian side, at El-Arish, close enough to serve as a staging ground. Joseph Chamberlain is interested in it. Herzl testifies before the Royal Commission on Alien Immigration in London and meets Lansdowne and Cromer in the same season. A survey goes out to the site and reports that the Nile water needed to make the desert arable cannot be spared. Cromer closes the file.
sources: Dossier, for the Royal Commission testimony and the British ministers, carried as reconstruction
suggested_refs: The El-Arish survey commission report, 1903, and Cromer's rejection

stops.name: Saint Petersburg, Plehve after Kishinev
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested; Wikipedia's 'Vyacheslav von Plehve' confirms August 1903, Saint Petersburg, and the substance of the exchange. The day is defaulted. The exact ministry building is not specified in the source and the coordinate is approximate.
stops.campa: In April a pogrom at Kishinev kills dozens over two days and empties whole streets, and the refugee question stops being an argument and becomes a queue. In August Herzl comes to Saint Petersburg and sits down with Vyacheslav von Plehve, the Interior Minister widely held responsible for the conditions that produced it, asking for legal recognition of Zionist organizing and Russian pressure on the Ottomans. Plehve forwards the proposals to the Tsar. Herzl is condemned across the Jewish world for having gone.
sources: Reviewed dossier, for the Kishinev pogrom of April 1903
suggested_refs: The Kishinev pogrom, April 1903, and the emigration crisis that followed it

stops.name: Basel, the Sixth Congress and East Africa
stops.date_confidence: the Sixth Congress ran 23 to 28 August 1903. The vote is partially confirmed: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Scheme gives 295 in favour and 178 against for sending a fact-finding group, but does NOT carry the 98 abstentions of the dossier, which is left out here, and describes the walkout as 'some Eastern European delegates' rather than Russians specifically. The attempted shooting of Max Nordau is in no fetched source and is omitted. Coordinate inherited as at the First Congress.
stops.campa: He puts the British offer of a territory in East Africa to the congress, not as a substitute for Palestine but as a night shelter for people who cannot wait for one. The vote to send an investigating commission carries, 295 to 178. Delegates from Eastern Europe walk out of the hall, the ones with most to gain from an immediate refuge refusing it hardest of all. The movement he assembled in this room six years ago has voted against its author. He goes out after them into the corridor.
stops.quote: We are one people--our enemies have made us one without our consent
stops.quote_source: The Jewish State (1896 translation), section 'Effects of Anti-Semitism'
sources: Jewish Virtual Library, excerpts from Der Judenstaat
ze_ev_jabotinsky.journey.json, which records a delegate's single sight of Herzl in this hall
suggested_refs: The Sixth Zionist Congress vote on the East Africa investigating commission, 295 to 178

stops.name: Rome, the Quirinal
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The audience with Victor Emmanuel III is carried from the dossier; neither the palace nor the precise date was confirmed by a fetched source. The day shown is chosen only to place the visit before the papal audience of 26 January.
stops.campa: Victor Emmanuel III receives him at the Quirinal and is cordial, informal, and interested. The king talks, asks questions, and offers nothing; Italy has no standing in Palestine and knows it. Herzl is working down the last unvisited courts on his list, because the list is what he has instead of a country, and in eight years of audiences no sovereign has given him a line of it in writing. He is forty-three. His heart will not carry him through the year.
sources: Dossier, carried as reconstruction; palace and date not independently confirmed
suggested_refs: The Quirinal Palace, Rome, seat of the Italian monarchy in 1904

stops.name: Rome, the Vatican and Pius X
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Wikipedia's 'Pope Pius X', which confirms the date, the Vatican location and the theological grounds for refusal. The reviewed dossier gives January 1904 without a day; the fetched chronology specifies the twenty-sixth.
stops.campa: Pius X receives him on the twenty-sixth of January and refuses him, plainly and without hostility. The Jews have not recognized Jesus, and so the Church cannot recognize the Jewish people's possession of the Holy Land; it would not, he adds, oppose civil protection for them there. It is the last audience of the campaign, and the only one at which the refusal is doctrinal rather than political. Herzl writes afterwards that he neither knelt nor kissed the Pope's hand.
suggested_refs: The Apostolic Palace audience of 26 January 1904

stops.name: Edlach, the death in the Rax valley
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; Wikipedia's 'Theodor Herzl' confirms Edlach and 3 July 1904. Coordinate corrected to Edlach an der Rax, 47.6925 N 15.808611 E, per de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edlach_an_der_Rax; that article documents the sanatorium founded 1898-99 but does not itself mention Herzl.
stops.campa: He dies at about five in the afternoon at Edlach, in the Rax valley, of cardiac sclerosis, in a sanatorium in the woods he had been sent to for rest. He is forty-four years old. The eight years behind him hold the pamphlet, six congresses, a bank, a newspaper he paid for himself, two approaches to a sultan, an audience with a kaiser and an audience with a pope, and a mileage nobody has ever totalled. He was married in this valley fifteen years before.
suggested_refs: The Sanatorium Edlach, Lower Austria, where Herzl died on 3 July 1904

stops.name: Vienna, the grave at Doebling
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the grave held the remains from 1904 to 1949. Coordinate corrected to the Doeblinger Friedhof at 48.238667 N 16.328139 E, resolving a contradiction between two lenses of this research, one of which gave a pin some 700 m off.
stops.campa: His will asked for the poorest class of funeral, no speeches and no flowers, and for him to lie beside his father until the Jewish people should carry his remains to Palestine. On the seventh of July he is buried at Doebling. The grave will hold him for forty-five years, and the clause of the will about Palestine stays open that long. The funeral is not poor: thousands come, from Vienna and from every country the movement has reached, and the procession outruns the arrangements made for it.
suggested_refs: The Herzl grave at the Doeblinger Friedhof, Vienna, 1904-1949

stops.name: Jerusalem, the hill that takes his name
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; Wikipedia's 'Mount Herzl' and 'Theodor Herzl' confirm the 1949 reinterment and the coordinates 31 degrees 46' 26" N, 35 degrees 10' 50" E. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from ze_ev_jabotinsky.journey.json, which pins the same hill; golda_meir.journey.json carries a different pin, 31.766, 35.15, and that divergence is left standing.
stops.campa: Fourteen months after independence, on the seventeenth of August, the remains are lifted out of Doebling and flown to Jerusalem with his parents and his sister Pauline, and buried on a hill at the western edge of the city which takes his name and becomes the national cemetery. The tomb is a plain block of black granite, chosen from sixty-three competition entries. The state's declaration had already named him in its own text: the spiritual father of the Jewish State.
stops.quote: The Jews who wish for a State will have it.
suggested_refs: Joseph Klarwein's black granite tomb on Mount Herzl, 1949
The 2006 reinterment of Pauline and Hans Herzl and the December 2007 reinterment of Stephen Norman on the same hill
